basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 18.' and it opens '(Vers. 18.) Et factum est cum dimitteret eam anima, siquidem moriebatur: vocavit nomen'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 18.) Et factum est cum dimitteret eam anima, siquidem moriebatur: vocavit nomen ejus, Filius doloris mei: pater vero ejus vocavit nomen ejus Benjamin. In Hebraeo similitudo nominis resonat; filius enim doloris mei, quod nomen moriens mater imposuit, dicitur BENONI (בן אוני). Filius vero dextrae, hoc est, virtutis, quod Jacob mutavit, appellatur BENJAMIM. Unde errant qui putant BENJAMIM (בנימין) filium dierum interpretari. Cum enim dextera appelletur JAMIN (ימין), et finiatur in n litteram: dies quidem appellantur et ipsi JAMIM (ימים), sed in m litteram terminantur.
